machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory, macOS 26.6.2
scope: Transformer startup: replace the no-copy QIPACK mapping with parallel F_NOCACHE pread into an ordinary shared Metal buffer; now the default, QI_DISABLE_PACK_PREAD=1 restores the mapping

diagnosis.release_build: CPU setup falls from about 75 to 15 ms; the 6.4-7.1 s first-dispatch cost is identical, so the debug build is not the bottleneck
diagnosis.cause: The first GPU dispatch touching the 14.2 GB no-copy buffer faults and wires the whole mapping at about 2 GB/s, even with a warm page cache

implementation: 8 threads, each one contiguous pack slice, positional reads through an F_NOCACHE descriptor into buffer.contents()

runs_in_order.note: about 5.1 GB swap in use; allocation competed with reclaim (13.05 s sys)

pipeline_1024_40_cache_dit_0_16.thermal_caveat: The A/B pair ran after about ten consecutive long GPU runs. Mapped full steps rose from 8.7 to 10.0 s during its run and the following pread run started there, so the loop difference is sustained-thermal ordering. The first pread run's full steps (8.62-8.78 s) match the best observed. Startup I/O is not GPU-clock bound and is the supported comparison.

result: Startup falls from about 6.6 s to about 2.3-2.6 s (about 4 s per image), or about 1 s under heavy swap pressure, with byte-identical output.
tradeoff: The weights count as process footprint (15.6-16.0 GB peak) instead of wired file-backed pages; physical residency is similar. The pack is no longer retained in the page cache between processes.
